figures.title: Phase of the AI journey organizations place themselves in
figures.subtitle: Senior leaders at organizations with US$50m+ revenue across 20 countries and territories, Q1 2026 (n=2,110) against Q2 2026 (n=2,145)
figures.quote: The largest movement this quarter occurred in the driving-adoption phase ... Which of the following best describes the phase your organization is in its AI journey? Q1 (n=2110), Q2 (n=2145)
figures.note: A quarterly executive survey: 2,145 senior leaders self-selecting a phase for their own organization, fielded online 28 April to 25 May 2026. Self-placement on a six-point maturity ladder is a judgement, not an audited measure — a leader claiming 'driving adoption' is not evidence AI is embedded at scale. The Q1 and Q2 waves are separate samples of respondents, not the same organizations tracked over time, so quarter-on-quarter shifts partly reflect sample composition. Percentages are rounded and sum to 100 within rounding.

figures.title: Senior leaders' confidence in AI, quarter on quarter
figures.subtitle: Share agreeing or strongly agreeing with three statements about AI, senior leaders across 20 countries and territories, Q1 2026 (n=2,110) against Q2 2026 (n=2,145)
figures.quote: Organizations are becoming more confident in AI's strategic value ... To what extent do you agree or disagree with the following statements? Percentage who agree/strongly agree Q1 (n=2110), Q2 (n=2145)
figures.unit: % of senior leaders who agree or strongly agree
figures.note: A quarterly executive survey of 2,145 senior leaders, fielded online 28 April to 25 May 2026. These are attitudes, not outcomes: 'AI is delivering meaningful business value' is a leader's own assessment, and KPMG defines it loosely as productivity gains, cost savings, revenue growth or better decision-making — the report separately shows only 7% claim established ROI. The two waves are separate samples, so the point changes are between-sample differences, not tracked change within the same firms.

figures.subtitle: Share naming each item a key AI priority, senior leaders across 20 countries and territories, Q1 2026 (n=2,110) against Q2 2026 (n=2,145)
figures.quote: AI priorities are expanding beyond productivity and efficiency ... Which of the following are key AI priorities for your organization? Q1 (n=2110), Q2 (n=2145)
figures.note: A quarterly executive survey of 2,145 senior leaders, fielded online 28 April to 25 May 2026. This is a multi-select question, so shares do not sum to 100 and a decline for one item can reflect crowding-out by newly salient items rather than any real fall in importance. Stated priorities are intentions reported by leaders, not budget allocations or observed activity. Q1 and Q2 are separate samples, not the same firms tracked.

figures.title: Who is ultimately accountable for business decisions informed by AI
figures.subtitle: Single answer given by senior leaders across 20 countries and territories, Q2 2026 (n=2,145)
figures.quote: Who is ultimately accountable for business decisions informed or executed using AI outputs? Q2 (n=2145)
figures.note: A quarterly executive survey of 2,145 senior leaders, fielded online 28 April to 25 May 2026. Answers describe who respondents believe is accountable — not a documented governance structure, and the report itself stresses that stated ownership and real accountability differ. Single-select, so shares sum to 100. Respondents are self-reporting on their own organization's governance, which invites flattering answers.

figures.title: Reported AI outcomes where the CEO is accountable against where they are not
figures.subtitle: Share strongly agreeing with each statement, split by whether the CEO is accountable for AI outcomes; senior leaders across 20 countries and territories, Q2 2026 (n=2,145)
figures.quote: The strongest outcomes are reported where accountability is clearly defined ... To what extent do you agree or disagree with the following statements? Percentage that strongly agree. Q2 (n=2145)
figures.note: A quarterly executive survey of 2,145 senior leaders, fielded online 28 April to 25 May 2026. This is a cross-sectional association, not evidence that clear accountability causes better outcomes — organizations further along with AI are plausibly both more likely to have assigned accountability and more likely to report returns. Both the split and the outcomes are self-reported by the same respondent, which inflates consistency. KPMG does not publish the sub-group sizes behind each split.

figures.title: How visible the operating costs of AI systems are
figures.subtitle: Single answer given by senior leaders across 20 countries and territories, Q2 2026 (n=2,145)
figures.quote: How visible are the operating costs of your AI systems today? Q2 (n=2145)
figures.note: A quarterly executive survey of 2,145 senior leaders, fielded online 28 April to 25 May 2026. Cost visibility is self-assessed — a leader saying costs are 'fully visible and actively monitored' is not the same as an audited cost-tracking capability, and the survey does not test the claim. Published percentages sum to 101 because of rounding. KPMG defines AI costs narrowly as the operating costs of AI systems today, which excludes build and capital costs.

figures.title: Whether organizations pulled back on AI agent deployment when costs outweighed value
figures.subtitle: Single answer given by senior leaders across 20 countries and territories, Q2 2026 (n=2,145)
figures.quote: Has your organization questioned, delayed, or scaled back the deployment of AI agents because the expected costs began to outweigh the value generated? Q2 (n=2145)
figures.note: A quarterly executive survey of 2,145 senior leaders, fielded online 28 April to 25 May 2026. Covers AI agents specifically, not AI spending overall, and the 5% who have not deployed agents are included in the base. The two 'yes' options sum to the 49% headline KPMG reports as having rephased deployments. Costs 'outweighing value' is the respondent's own judgement — no cost or return figures are collected — and only 35% of the same sample report full visibility into what AI costs them.
